entities.summary: The Lerma Ducal Palace is the palace of the dukes of Lerma in Lerma (Burgos) in Spain, occupying the whole of one side of the city's Plaza. Originally it had immense gardens below it, on the banks of the river, with fountains, stately homes and seven chapels, of which one (Cristo) remains. All documents relating to its construction have been conserved. A 17th-century work, building started in 1601 under commission from Francisco Gómez de Sandoval y Rojas, Duke of Lerma. Its architect was Francisco de Mora and is it is considered de Mora's masterwork and one of the finest buildings of that era.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Lerma Ducal Palace played a significant role in the architectural history of Spain during the 17th century, showcasing the work of renowned architect Francisco de Mora. Its construction had a lasting impact on the region's cultural heritage.
